description: A high-throughput, low-latency hyper-local food delivery platform architecture supporting real-time order matching, geospatial driver tracking, dynamic pricing, and multi-tenant restaurant catalog management.

microservices.name: API Gateway Service
microservices.responsibility: Handles entry point request routing, SSL termination, rate limiting, JWT validation, and client API versioning.

microservices.name: Identity & Auth Service
microservices.responsibility: Manages user profiles, role-based access control (Customers, Drivers, Restaurant Admins), OAuth2/OIDC, and session management.

microservices.name: Restaurant & Menu Service
microservices.responsibility: Manages restaurant onboarding, menu items, dynamic inventory availability, operating hours, and localized pricing models.

microservices.name: Order Lifecycle Service
microservices.responsibility: Orchestrates order creation, state machine transitions (Pending, Accepted, Preparing, Dispatched, Delivered), and cart validation.

microservices.name: Delivery & Tracking Service
microservices.responsibility: Handles real-time geospatial driver location tracking, order-driver dispatch matching algorithms, dynamic ETA calculation, and WebSocket connections.

microservices.name: Payment & Ledger Service
microservices.responsibility: Integrates payment gateways (Stripe, PayPal), manages customer refunds, processes driver payouts, and maintains double-entry transaction ledgers.

microservices.name: Notification & Messaging Service
microservices.responsibility: Dispatches cross-channel push notifications (FCM, APNS), SMS alerts (Twilio), and email updates based on system event triggers.

databases.justification: Used for ultra-fast rate-limiting bucket storage, token revocation lookup, and request routing cache.
Provides strong ACID compliance and relational integrity for user credentials, roles, and profile information.
Flexible document model simplifies handling complex nested menu structures, dynamic modifiers, and frequent menu updates.
Guarantees strict transactional consistency and isolation required for order state management, pricing records, and tax calculations.
Redis In-Memory Geo Spatials handle ephemeral sub-second driver location updates; PostGIS persists historical delivery routes and zone boundaries.
Ensures financial-grade transactional safety, row-level locking, and immutable audit trailing for payment records.
Stores un-structured notification templates, user communication preferences, and delivery log histories.

communication.justification: Synchronous request/response required to instantly validate carts and return preliminary order IDs to clients.
Synchronous payment authorization required before committing an order to the active lifecycle state.
Asynchronously emits 'OrderReadyForPickup' events so dispatch systems can immediately begin driver matching without blocking order APIs.
Decouples location update streaming from push notification dispatching during proximity alerts (e.g., driver arrived).
Asynchronously publishes 'PaymentSettled' or 'PaymentFailed' events to trigger order confirmation or cancellation workflows.

endpoints.description: Proxies client authentication request to Identity Service and returns JWT.
Proxies geolocation query parameters to obtain nearby open restaurants.
Creates a new order draft, computes final taxes/fees, and reserves inventory.
Retrieves the detailed status and current timeline of a specific order.
Updates order state (e.g., accepted by restaurant, in kitchen).
Ingests high-frequency coordinates from the driver mobile app.
Gets current driver location and real-time calculated ETA for customer apps.
Processes payment auth via external processor.
Receives asynchronous status callbacks from external payment gateways.

technology_stack.frontend: React Native (iOS/Android Client & Driver Apps), React.js (Restaurant Partner Dashboard)
technology_stack.backend: Go (Gin, Fiber), Java (Spring Boot), Node.js (NestJS), Python (FastAPI)
technology_stack.database: PostgreSQL (with PostGIS extension), MongoDB Atlas, Redis Cluster
technology_stack.deployment: AWS EKS (Kubernetes), Docker, Terraform, Helm, ArgoCD, Datadog

deployment_notes: Deploy microservices as containerized deployments on AWS EKS across 3 Availability Zones for high availability.
Utilize Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) driven by custom Prometheus metrics (e.g., HTTP request rates and Kafka consumer group lag).
Implement Istio Service Mesh for mutual TLS (mTLS) security between internal microservices and fine-grained traffic management.
Use Redis Enterprise with multi-region replication for ultra-low latency driver location caching and token management.
Establish CI/CD pipelines via GitHub Actions and ArgoCD for GitOps-driven deployment to staging and production clusters.

strengths: Excellent use of Polyglot Persistence selecting PostGIS for spatial tracking, MongoDB for dynamic menus, and PostgreSQL for financial/order ACID isolation.
Event-driven architecture using Kafka prevents system blocking during high concurrency peak order hours (e.g., lunch/dinner spikes).
Strong operational separation between real-time driver tracking and core order orchestration microservices.
weaknesses: Multiple programming languages (Go, Java, Node.js, Python) increase operational overhead, developer context switching, and CI/CD complexity for an early-stage team.
High reliance on Managed Kafka and multi-node Kubernetes clusters increases baseline monthly infrastructure spend.
recommendations: Standardize backend languages to max two (e.g., Go for high-throughput performance services like Delivery/Gateway, Node.js/TypeScript for business logic services like Auth/Orders) during MVP phase.
Implement a Circuit Breaker pattern (e.g., using Resilience4j or Istio) on the Payment service link to gracefully handle gateway degradation.
Introduce a dead-letter queue (DLQ) pattern on Kafka streams for failed notification and payout executions to ensure zero data loss.
